common_name: Moonglow Rocky Mountain Juniper (Silvery-Blue Columnar Screening Conifer)

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in well-drained, average to dry soil in full sun; Moonglow is a vigorous, broadly columnar juniper that tolerates heat and drought once established.

directions: Moonglow is a seedling selection of Rocky Mountain juniper found in the 1970s at Hillside Nursery in Lehighton, Pennsylvania and later brought into wide release by Monrovia Nursery. It forms a dense, upright, narrowly pyramidal column noticeably broader and fuller than slimmer blue junipers like 'Skyrocket,' clothed in intensely silvery-blue scale-like foliage that holds its glowing color through every season. Plant in full sun in well-drained soil, where its vigorous growth rate quickly builds a tall accent, informal screen, or windbreak; established plants shrug off heat, cold, and extended drought with little care. Give it room to fill out its broader-than-'Skyrocket' width, and site with good air movement to limit the fungal twig blight that can trouble junipers in humid climates.

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, sheltered from drying winter wind.

directions: Gracilis, sometimes sold as slender hinoki falsecypress, is a larger-growing, narrowly pyramidal hinoki cypress selection, distinct from the smaller, more tightly mounded 'Nana Gracilis' that is often confused with it in nursery catalogs. Its tiny, deep green, fan-shaped sprays carry a soft, ferny texture and pick up a bronze cast in winter cold, while the plant builds slowly into an upright small tree rather than staying dwarf. Grow in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade, since like other hinoki cypress selections it resents both drought and waterlogged ground. Little pruning is needed beyond removing dead interior growth, and its narrow profile suits it to specimen use or screening where a full-sized hinoki cypress would be too broad.
sources: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Nigra Dark American Arborvitae (Dark Green Winter-Hardy Arborvitae)

planting.note: Plant in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade, spacing for a hedge or screen if wanted.

directions: Nigra, also sold as Dark American arborvitae, is an old American selection of eastern arborvitae documented as far back as the 1930s, grown for exceptionally dark green scale-like foliage that holds its color through winter far better than the straight species, which often bronzes in cold weather. It builds at an intermediate pace into a narrow, dense, pyramidal to columnar shrub useful for hedges, screens, and foundation plantings in cold-winter climates. Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; like other arborvitae it is best suited to cooler northern gardens and struggles with the heat and humidity of the Deep South. Its reliable dark color and hardiness have also made it a parent plant in later arborvitae breeding programs.
sources: L.H. Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture (1933)
